Common Reselling Costs Beginners Forget

A practical checklist for expenses that quietly reduce profit.

Small costs become material when repeated across many orders. Commonly missed item-level expenses include packaging, seller-paid postage, promoted listings, cleaning supplies, repair parts, authentication, and fixed transaction charges.

Separate direct and shared costs

Direct costs belong to one item. Shared costs—software, storage, equipment, and mileage—support the broader business. Track both, but avoid counting the same expense twice.

  • Purchase price and inbound shipping
  • Selling and payment fees
  • Outbound shipping and insurance
  • Boxes, mailers, tape, labels, and void fill
  • Cleaning, testing, repair, or replacement parts
  • Advertising and promotion
  • Returns, refunds, and damaged shipments

Start with the profit calculator, then save a consistent cost checklist for every listing.

Keep the estimate honest.

Fee structures and actual costs can change. Verify the rules that apply to your sale and treat every result as planning information.
